title: Probabilistic slot groomer with temporal hints to reduce KV fragmentation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Introduce a lightweight 'probabilistic slot groomer' daemon that continuously heals KV cache fragmentation using temporal locality hints and bounded background compaction. Goals: (1) reduce long-tail memory waste from slot fragmentation, (2) avoid pause-y compaction that harms tail latency during high batching rates, (3) operate within GPU memory and kernel scheduling constraints.
description_2: Design overview: We track approximate per-slot access recency using a compact 8-bit aging counter and an approximate hit sketch (count-min / small bloom-style fingerprint per microstripe). Rather than global compaction passes, the groomer performs micro-grafts: it probabilistically selects underutilized slots within a micro-epoch (aligned to continuous-batching windows) and attempts a cheap in-place slot coalescing or pointer remap. Hot slots (recently accessed or with high sketch counts) are skipped to avoid moving live KV state. A small reservoir of candidate slots is maintained per-GPU and per-model to localize activity and prevent cross-model interference.
description_3: Integration with continuous batching: Grooming work is budgeted as a fraction of the batching lane CPU/GPU time slice. We align micro-epochs with the batching window (configurable; default 50ms) so grooming tends to run between heavy token generation bursts. When observed p99 latency increases or batching backlog grows, groomer automatically reduces its budget to zero and reclaims the budget incrementally when load subsides.
description_4: GPU memory optimizations: To minimize copies and CUDA synchronization, the groomer prefers pointer table updates with atomic swap and uses page-aligned slot layouts to enable single memcpy for coalesced regions. We use compacted metadata stored in pinned host memory for fast decision-making and batch small relocations into a single kernel to amortize launch cost. For quantized KV values we store relocation maps that avoid decompressing values during move operations.
description_5: Safety and correctness: Relocations use an epoched two-phase publish (reserve -> move -> swap -> retire) that allows in-flight requests to consult both old and new locations via a lightweight indirection layer. We provide fallbacks to conservative eviction when compaction cannot safely proceed under contention.
description_6: Telemetry and metrics: New metrics: groomer_budget_pct, groomer_relocations/sec, groomer_failed_moves, avg_slot_fragmentation_ratio, fragmentable_bytes, reloc_bytes_amortized. We'll add traces linking relocations to request ids for debugging mis-attribution of latency.
description_7: Testing plan: unit tests for epoched publish, simulation harness with synthetic access traces (zipfian + temporal bursts), GPU soak tests with continuous-batching enabled, and canary rollout to a small subset of Dedicated nodes. Benchmark targets: reduce fragmentable_bytes by 40% within 1 minute of steady-state on synthetic workload without increasing p99 token latency by >1ms.
description_8: Rollout plan: feature flag gated; start with "groomer=off" default, enable in internal canary, monitor metrics and error rates for 72h, then enable for low-priority tenants, progressively widen. Provide a console toggle and an autoscale policy to limit groomer CPU/GPU budget.
comments: 2026-03-02 | Ava Martinez: Initial spike completed. Prototype demonstrates >3x reduction in small-slot fragmentation on synthetic traces. Observed some increased kernel launches when relocation batch size=1; moving to batch size=8 reduced overhead.

2026-03-04 | Liam O'Connor: Reviewed epoched publish design. Concern: GC of retired pointers needs stronger bounds to avoid leak. Action: add per-epoch grace counters and integrate with existing GC fence in runtime.
2026-03-06 | Priya Desai (PM): Aligning on SLO: keep p99 generation latency increase <=1ms for Hosted tier. Also requested console metric surfaces for fragmentable_bytes and reloc_bytes_amortized.

2026-03-08 | Eng-Infra review by Mateo Alvarez: Suggested using cudamemadvise for read-mostly pages and consolidating pinned metadata into a single struct to reduce host-GPU transfers. Accepted with follow-up PR.

2026-03-10 | QA: Added stability test plan and an initial failure-mode doc: if relocation fails due to OOM, groomer will mark region "sticky-frag" and back off exponentially, reporting to ops channel.
